assumptions_not_in_consensus.commissioning_years: U(1, 2) from 0B start to the first product departing the NEA (not in consensus)
assumptions_not_in_consensus.site_power_mass_t: log-uniform 60–550 t for 2–8 MW at the NEA (consensus gives no mass; GPT placeholder 550 t)
assumptions_not_in_consensus.spares_import_t_per_yr: U(20, 60) t/yr (bom-0-14 gives cost, not mass)
assumptions_not_in_consensus.earth_material_cost_per_kg: U(50, 500) $/kg for the Earth-made equivalent product before launch
assumptions_not_in_consensus.site_cargo_outbound_t: U(0, 20) t per tug trip (spares and consumables on the outbound leg)
assumptions_not_in_consensus.tug_scaling_with_power: 55% of tug dry mass and unit cost scales with installed power, 45% is fixed (not in consensus)
assumptions_not_in_consensus.leg_feasibility_at_other_thrust: an optimised leg stays flyable if its thrust fraction fits the modelled tug's acceleration (0.95 margin); its Δv is not re-optimised, and legs infeasible in the study are never added back
assumptions_not_in_consensus.tug_life_years: U(10, 15): Claude and GPT carry a 15-year objective, Gemini states none; replacement is pro rata for the years beyond that life
assumptions_not_in_consensus.plant_life_years: U(10, 15) (bom-0-3 design life); 40–70% of plant cost and mass is replaced at end of life (not in consensus)
assumptions_not_in_consensus.robot_attrition_per_yr: U(0.3, 0.7) robots a year beyond the first 6.25 years (from 2–4 replacements on 6 active in bom-0-2)
assumptions_not_in_consensus.not_replaced: site power, the SEL1 node and the propellant yard are assumed to last 20 years
assumptions_not_in_consensus.run_rate_0b_lines: ops, spares and comms 0B lines rescaled from the run length their consensus priced (6.25, 5 and 7 yr) to the drawn run
